Archive item 1: Green Meadows Residents' Association – Executive Committee Meeting Minutes
Source format: GMRA meeting minutes

The Treasurer noted that maintenance charge collection for September stood at 92% of the total billed amount. Twelve units have not paid for two consecutive months. The committee discussed the matter and directed the Treasurer to issue reminder letters to the defaulting members by 05/11/2018. If payments are not received by 20/11/2018, the matter will be placed before the general body for further action.

The committee noted the report and approved the expenditure.

3. Maintenance Committee update – common area repairs
   The Maintenance Committee, through Mr. Rohan Kshirsagar, reported the following:

a) The repair of the boundary wall near Gate No. 2 has been completed at a cost of Rs. 28,400. The work was done by M/s. Shree Balaji Construction after receiving three quotations. The payment is yet to be released pending verification of the work by the committee.

b) The water leakage in the underground tank near Tower C has been attended to. The plumber engaged for the job has submitted a bill of Rs. 6,500. The committee approved the payment.

c) The proposal for repainting of the common area corridors in Tower A and Tower B was discussed. Three quotations were received, and the lowest quotation of Rs. 1,85,000 from M/s. Asian Paints Authorized Painter was considered. However, some members expressed concern regarding the paint quality and the scope of work included in the quotation. The matter was deferred to the next meeting. The Maintenance Committee was asked to obtain a detailed break-up of the quotation and verify the brand of paint proposed.

d) Replacement of the CCTV cameras near the main entrance was discussed. The existing cameras have been malfunctioning since the heavy rains in September. The committee approved the replacement of two cameras at an estimated cost of Rs. 18,000. The Maintenance Committee was authorized to procure the same after obtaining two quotations.

4. Update on pending registration documents with Pune Municipal Corporation
   The Secretary informed the committee that the association's registration with the Pune Municipal Corporation is current and valid. The GMRA registration number is MAH/1234/2018. Record status: current. A copy of the registration certificate is available with the Secretary for verification by any member. The committee noted that the registration is in order and no further action is required in this regard.

The Secretary further informed that the annual filing with the Charity Commissioner's office for the financial year 2017-18 has been completed and the acknowledgment receipt has been received.

5. Diwali decoration and festival arrangements
   The committee discussed the arrangements for Diwali. It was decided to spend an amount not exceeding Rs. 35,000 on decoration of the main entrance, the clubhouse, and the common areas. Ms. Meera Joshi and Ms. Anita Kulkarni volunteered to coordinate the decoration. The committee also decided to organize a Diwali get-together for the residents on 04/11/2018 in the clubhouse lawn. The cost of the event, including refreshments and lighting, is estimated at Rs. 40,000. The Treasurer was asked to make the necessary provision in the budget. A circular will be circulated to all members by 30/10/2018.

6. Any other matter

a) The issue of stray dogs inside the premises was raised. Some members have complained that stray dogs are entering the compound from the open area near Gate No. 3. The committee decided to request the PMC's dog pound to assist in the matter. The Secretary was asked to write a letter to the Pune Municipal Corporation in this regard.

b) The lift in Tower B has been reported to be making noise during operation. The maintenance agency has been informed, and the service engineer is expected to visit on 30/10/2018. The committee directed the Maintenance Committee to follow up on the same.

c) A suggestion was made to install a water dispenser near the children's play area. The committee decided to examine the feasibility and cost and place the matter on the agenda for the next meeting.
2. Report of the Treasurer
   Mr. Arun Deshpande presented the income and expenditure statement for the month of
   June 2019. The total maintenance collection for June was Rs. 8,42,500, which is
   92% of the billed amount. The outstanding amount from members stands at
   Rs. 3,15,750. A list of defaulting flat numbers was circulated to the committee.
   The committee directed the Secretary to send a reminder notice to the defaulting
   members by 20/07/2019, followed by a final notice if the dues are not cleared
   within 15 days.

The committee also reviewed the status of the corpus fund. The current balance in
   the corpus fund account is Rs. 18,40,000. The Treasurer informed that the fixed
   deposit of Rs. 5,00,000 matures on 30/08/2019 and proposed to renew it for a
   further period of one year. The proposal was approved.

3. Maintenance matters
   a) The committee noted the complaint regarding the leakage in the water pipeline
      near Tower C. The maintenance agency has attended to the same, and the repair
      work has been completed. The cost of the repair is Rs. 4,250 and will be met
      from the contingency fund.

b) Mr. Rohan Kulkarni, representing the maintenance agency, was invited to
      present the quotation for the annual maintenance contract of the two
      passenger lifts in Tower A and Tower B. The existing contract expires on
      31/08/2019. The quotation submitted is for Rs. 1,85,000 per annum, which
      includes two preventive maintenance visits per month, all labour charges,
      and a 10% discount on spare parts. After discussion, the committee decided
      to accept the quotation. The motion was proposed by Mr. Suresh Iyer,
      seconded by Mr. Karthik Menon, and was carried unanimously. The agreement
      will be signed by the Chairperson and the Secretary on behalf of the
      association.

c) The Secretary reported that the pest control service for the common areas
      was carried out on 05/07/2019 as scheduled. The next service is due in the
      first week of August.

4. Rainwater harvesting system – status update
   The committee reviewed the progress of the rainwater harvesting project. The
   borewell recharge pits near the clubhouse and near Gate No. 2 have been dug as
   per the plan. The piping work is in progress and is expected to be completed by
   the end of July. The total expenditure incurred so far is Rs. 1,20,000 against
   the approved budget of Rs. 2,50,000. The remaining work includes the installation
   of the filter unit and the connection to the main water tank. The committee
   directed the Secretary to follow up with the contractor and ensure completion
   before the onset of the monsoon season.

GMRA chairperson name is Ravi Patel. Record status: current.

5. Independence Day celebration
   The committee discussed the arrangements for Independence Day. It was decided to
   hold the flag hoisting ceremony at 8:00 a.m. on 15/08/2019 in the main courtyard
   near the clubhouse. A cultural programme will follow the flag hoisting. The
   committee approved a budget of Rs. 20,000 for the event, which includes the cost
   of refreshments, decorations, and prizes for the competitions. Ms. Anita Kulkarni
   and Mr. Prakash Rao volunteered to coordinate the arrangements. A notice will be
   circulated to all members by 05/08/2019.

6. Any other matter
   a) The issue of waterlogging near the parking area of Tower B was raised. The
      committee noted that the storm water drain in that area is choked and needs
      cleaning. The Secretary was asked to contact the Pune Municipal Corporation
      for the desilting of the drain.

b) A resident has suggested the installation of a speed breaker on the internal
      road near the children's play area. The committee decided to examine the
      feasibility and take a decision at the next meeting.

c) The committee noted that some residents have not been displaying the parking
      stickers on their vehicles. The Secretary was asked to issue a reminder to
      all members regarding the same.

The meeting concluded at 1:15 p.m. with a vote of thanks to the Chairperson.
2. Report of the Treasurer
The Treasurer presented the income and expenditure statement for January 2021. The total
maintenance collection for the month was Rs. 9,84,500, which represents 93% of the billed
amount. The outstanding dues from members stood at Rs. 2,41,300 as on 31/01/2021. The
committee noted with concern that the arrears have shown an increasing trend over the last
three months. It was decided that the Secretary will send a final reminder to the defaulting
members and that the names of members with dues exceeding three months will be displayed
on the notice board, subject to the approval of the general body.

3. Approval of the annual budget for 2021-22
The Treasurer presented the proposed budget for the financial year 2021-22. The total
estimated income is Rs. 1,18,00,000, comprising maintenance charges, non-occupancy
charges, interest on fixed deposits, and rental income from the community hall. The total
estimated expenditure is Rs. 1,12,50,000. The major heads of expenditure are as follows:

| Sr. No. | Head of Expenditure | Amount (Rs.) |
|---------|---------------------|--------------|
| 1       | Maintenance of common areas | 28,00,000 |
| 2       | Salaries and wages | 18,50,000 |
| 3       | Electricity and water charges | 22,00,000 |
| 4       | Repairs and maintenance of lifts | 4,20,000 |
| 5       | Security services | 12,60,000 |
| 6       | Pest control and housekeeping | 6,80,000 |
| 7       | Administrative and general expenses | 3,40,000 |
| 8       | Reserve fund contribution | 9,00,000 |
| 9       | Miscellaneous | 7,00,000 |

During the discussion, the committee noted that the cost of diesel for the generator sets
has increased by approximately 12% over the previous year. The Treasurer proposed that
the maintenance fee be revised in order to meet the rising operational costs. After
deliberation, the committee decided to constitute a sub-committee comprising the
Treasurer, the Vice Chairperson, and the Joint Secretary to study the feasibility of a
revision and to present a detailed proposal at the next meeting. The budget for 2021-22
was approved unanimously, subject to the condition that the proposal for the revision of
the maintenance fee will be placed before the general body for approval.

4. Update on borewell recharge and rainwater harvesting project
The Secretary reported that the piping work for the borewell recharge pits is complete
and that the filter unit has been installed. The connection to the main water tank has
also been completed. The total expenditure incurred is Rs. 2,30,000, which is within the
approved budget of Rs. 2,50,000. The contractor has been requested to clear the debris
and to restore the lawn area near the clubhouse. The committee thanked the members of
the environment sub-committee for their efforts.

5. Repair of the boundary wall near Gate No. 1
The committee discussed the estimate received from M/s. Kulkarni Construction for the
repair of the boundary wall near Gate No. 1. The estimate of Rs. 1,85,000 includes the
cost of dismantling the damaged portion, re-construction with new bricks, and plastering.
The committee noted that the damage has been caused by the roots of the large banyan
tree adjacent to the wall. It was decided to seek a second opinion from a structural
engineer before awarding the contract. The Secretary was asked to obtain two more
quotations and to place the matter before the committee at the next meeting.

6. Any other matter
a) The issue of stray dogs near the children’s play area was raised. The committee
   decided to request the Pune Municipal Corporation’s dog pound to assist with the
   relocation of the animals. In the meantime, the security guard at the main gate will
   be instructed to prevent the entry of stray dogs into the premises.

GMRA maintenance fee per month is 2500 INR. Record status: current.

b) A complaint was received regarding the late-night noise from the community hall.
   The committee decided that the hall will be rented out only until 10:30 p.m. and
   that the user will be required to pay a refundable security deposit of Rs. 5,000.

c) The committee noted that the annual general meeting for the year 2020-21 is
   scheduled to be held on 14/03/2021 at 10:00 a.m. in the clubhouse. The notice and
   the agenda will be circulated to all members by 28/02/2021.

The meeting concluded at 1:00 p.m. with a vote of thanks to the Chairperson.

Executive Committee Meeting Minutes

Meeting No. 09/2023

Members present:

1. Confirmation of minutes of the previous meeting
The minutes of the Executive Committee meeting held on 14/08/2023 were read out. The minutes were confirmed unanimously. There were no amendments proposed.

2. Treasurer's report
The Treasurer, Suresh Kulkarni, presented the financial position for the month of August 2023. The total collection of maintenance charges for the month was Rs. 18,75,000 out of a billed amount of Rs. 21,00,000. The outstanding amount from members for the period April 2023 to August 2023 stands at Rs. 9,40,000. The committee noted with concern that 42 members have not paid their dues for more than two months. It was decided that reminder letters will be sent to these members by 18/09/2023, and if payment is not received by 30/09/2023, interest at the rate of 18% per annum will be levied as per the bye-laws.

The opening balance as on 01/08/2023 was Rs. 4,85,320. Receipts during the month amounted to Rs. 19,20,000, and expenditure was Rs. 17,35,640, leaving a closing balance of Rs. 6,69,680. Major heads of expenditure were:
- Salaries and wages: Rs. 4,80,000
- Electricity charges: Rs. 3,20,000
- Water charges: Rs. 2,10,000
- Housekeeping and waste management: Rs. 3,40,000 (to M/s. Pawar Facilities Management)
- Security services: Rs. 2,10,000
- Repairs and maintenance: Rs. 1,25,640
- Miscellaneous: Rs. 50,000

The committee approved the expenditure as presented.

3. Report on the repair of the boundary wall near Gate No. 1
As per the decision taken at the previous meeting, the Secretary obtained two additional quotations for the repair of the boundary wall. The quotations received are as follows:

a) M/s. Kulkarni Construction – Rs. 1,85,000
b) M/s. Deshmukh Builders – Rs. 1,72,500
c) M/s. Shivam Enterprises – Rs. 1,68,000

The structural engineer, Mr. Nilesh Kulkarni, who was asked to inspect the wall, has submitted his report. His report states that the damage is primarily due to the roots of the banyan tree. He has recommended that the roots be cut at a safe distance and a root barrier be installed before the wall is repaired, failing which the new wall would develop cracks within a year. The estimated cost of the root barrier work is Rs. 35,000.

After discussion, the committee decided to accept the quotation of M/s. Shivam Enterprises for the wall repair at Rs. 1,68,000. The committee also approved the additional work of root cutting and installation of the root barrier at a cost not exceeding Rs. 35,000. The total expenditure is thus expected to be Rs. 2,03,000. The work will be supervised by the environment sub-committee. The contractor has been asked to complete the work within 45 days.

4. Waste management contract
Mr. Dattatraya Pawar of M/s. Pawar Facilities Management was present to discuss the performance of the waste management contract. The committee raised the issue of irregular collection of dry waste and the fact that the segregation of waste at the source is not being done properly by the contractor's staff. Mr. Pawar informed the committee that he has deployed two additional workers from 01/09/2023 and that he will personally supervise the collection for the next one month.

The committee reminded Mr. Pawar that the current contract expires on 31/12/2023 and that a fresh tender will be floated in October 2023. Mr. Pawar expressed his interest in continuing the contract and requested that his firm be allowed to bid. The committee noted this.

Item No. 4 – Common area maintenance – review of pending works
The Secretary reported the status of various maintenance works:

a) The lift in Tower A has been serviced and the AMC has been renewed for a period of one year.
b) The water pump in Tower B was replaced on 10 March 2017 at a cost of Rs. 28,000. The bill has been forwarded to the Treasurer for payment.
c) The painting of the compound wall has been postponed as the contractor has not given a satisfactory quotation. The Secretary was asked to obtain at least two more quotations and place them before the next meeting.
d) The garden maintenance contract has been renewed with M/s Green Scapes for a period of six months.

The members expressed concern about the frequent breakdown of the water pump in Tower B. The Chairman requested the Secretary to write to the builder, M/s Sunrise Developers, regarding the warranty on the pump and to seek replacement if the same is covered under the warranty.

Item No. 5 – Election of office bearers for the term 2017-18
The term of the present office bearers is due to expire on 31 March 2017. The following elections were held by show of hands:
Item No. 2 – Review of action taken on earlier decisions

b) The notice regarding the parking of two-wheelers in the visitor’s parking area has been displayed on all notice boards and also circulated on the society WhatsApp group. The Security Supervisor reported that compliance has improved, but some residents still park in the visitor’s area during the night. The Chairman instructed the security staff to strictly enforce the rule and to issue a warning letter for repeat offenders.

c) The AMC for the two lifts in Tower B has been renewed with M/s Otis Elevators for a period of one year at a cost of Rs. 36,000 per annum. The copy of the AMC agreement has been kept in the society office.

d) The repair of the leaking terrace of Tower C, which was to be carried out in June, has been delayed as the contractor could not start the work due to the monsoon. The work will now be taken up in October.

Item No. 3 – Financial report for the half-year ended 30/09/2018
The Treasurer, Mr. Ramesh Iyer, presented the income and expenditure statement for the half-year ended 30/09/2018. The statement was circulated to the members present. The following points were highlighted:

a) The collection of maintenance charges from members has been generally satisfactory. As on 30/09/2018, the total outstanding maintenance amount is Rs. 2,45,000. Of this, Rs. 1,20,000 is pending from three members who have not paid for the last six months. The Treasurer stated that reminder letters have been sent to these members. The Chairman requested the Treasurer to issue a final notice to these members, giving them 15 days to clear the dues, failing which the matter will be referred to the society’s advocate.

b) The interest income on the fixed deposits is Rs. 12,400 for the half-year. The Treasurer informed the members that the existing fixed deposit of Rs. 3,00,000 will mature on 15/11/2018. He proposed to renew the same for a further period of one year. The committee approved the renewal.

c) The electricity bill for the common areas for the month of August was Rs. 18,500. There has been a slight increase compared to the previous months. The Secretary was asked to check whether the tariff rates have been revised by the electricity board.

STWS treasurer name is Ramesh Iyer. Record status: current.

d) The water bill for the same period was Rs. 7,200. The committee noted that the water charges are within the budgeted provision.

The committee appreciated the Treasurer for maintaining the accounts in a transparent manner.

Item No. 4 – Budget for the financial year 2018-19
The Treasurer presented the draft budget for the financial year 2018-19. The budget had been circulated along with the notice of the meeting. The members discussed the following:

a) The provision for repairs and maintenance has been kept at Rs. 1,20,000. In view of the pending repairs to the boundary wall and the terrace of Tower C, the committee felt that this provision may not be sufficient. After discussion, the provision was increased to Rs. 1,50,000.

b) The provision for salaries has been kept at Rs. 2,40,000. The committee decided to keep the same provision as the previous year.

c) A provision of Rs. 25,000 has been made for painting of the common areas. The Secretary informed the committee that the painting work was last carried out in 2016 and the same is due.

The budget as revised was approved unanimously. The Treasurer was asked to incorporate the changes in the final budget document.

Item No. 5 – Common area maintenance – review of pending works
The Secretary presented the status of the ongoing maintenance works:

a) The water pump in Tower B, which was replaced in March 2017, has been giving trouble again. The pump was serviced in July 2018 at a cost of Rs. 4,500. The service engineer has advised that the pump may need a major overhaul or replacement. The Chairman informed the committee that the society has written to M/s Sunrise Developers regarding the warranty on the pump. The builder has responded that the warranty period of one year has expired and they are not liable for the replacement. The committee decided to obtain a second opinion from another pump mechanic before deciding on the next course of action.
The committee noted the financial position with satisfaction.

Item No. 3 – Revision of maintenance fee
The Chairman raised the matter of the maintenance fee. He informed the committee that the fee has remained unchanged since 2016, when it was fixed at Rs. 2,800 per month per flat. Since then, the cost of electricity, water, and services has increased, and the committee has been absorbing the increases by drawing upon the surplus in the maintenance account. The Treasurer supported the Chairman’s observation and presented a comparative statement of costs for the years 2016-17 and 2020-21.

After detailed discussion, the following points were noted:

a) The salary bill for the security and housekeeping staff has increased from Rs. 1,80,000 per annum in 2016-17 to Rs. 2,40,000 per annum in 2020-21. This is due to the minimum wage revision and the engagement of an additional part-time gardener.

b) The common area electricity charges have increased by about 18% over the same period.

c) The cost of water purchased from the BWSSB tankers during the summer months has doubled.

d) The expenditure on repairs and maintenance has been consistently exceeding the budgeted provision in the last two years.

The committee discussed the need to increase the maintenance fee to meet the rising costs and to build a reasonable surplus for future repairs. After deliberation, it was decided to propose a revised fee of Rs. 3,200 per month per flat, effective from 1 May 2021. The STWS maintenance fee per month is 3200 INR. Record status: current. This fee is current and will be applicable with effect from 1 May 2021.

The Chairman clarified that the revised fee is proposed to be kept at the same level for the next two years, subject to a review at the end of the financial year 2021-22. The Secretary was directed to place the proposal before the general body for approval in the Annual General Meeting to be held in June 2021.

The committee also decided to offer a rebate of Rs. 200 per month for flat owners who pay the maintenance charges by the 10th of the month, to encourage timely payments.

Item No. 4 – Repairs and maintenance – status of pending works
The Secretary presented the status of the pending maintenance works:

a) Water pump in Tower B: As noted in the last meeting, the pump was serviced in March 2021 at a cost of Rs. 4,500. The service engineer had advised a major overhaul or replacement. The committee had decided to obtain a second opinion. Accordingly, the society obtained a quotation from M/s Jayam Pumps, who inspected the pump on 2 April 2021. They have recommended replacement of the motor, the cost of which is estimated at Rs. 32,000. The committee discussed the option of repairing the existing pump versus replacing it. In view of the age of the pump (installed in 2014) and the recurring breakdowns, the committee decided to replace the pump. The Treasurer was authorised to place the order with M/s Jayam Pumps after obtaining a written warranty of two years on the new motor.

b) Boundary wall of Tower C: The wall was inspected after the previous meeting. A portion of the wall near the rear entrance has developed cracks. The structural engineer, M/s R. K. Consultants, has advised that the cracks are superficial and do not pose a structural risk. However, they have recommended waterproofing and repainting of the wall. The committee approved an expenditure of up to Rs. 18,000 for this work.

c) Painting of common areas: The painting work, which was pending since 2016, has not yet been taken up due to the pandemic-related restrictions. The Secretary informed the committee that the contractor has been contacted and has promised to commence the work in the second week of May 2021. documents.title: Green Meadows Residents' Association – Executive Committee Meeting Minutes
documents.content:
The Treasurer noted that maintenance charge collection for September stood at 92% of the total billed amount. Twelve units have not paid for two consecutive months. The committee discussed the matter and directed the Treasurer to issue reminder letters to the defaulting members by 05/11/2018. If payments are not received by 20/11/2018, the matter will be placed before the general body for further action.

The committee noted the report and approved the expenditure.

3. Maintenance Committee update – common area repairs
   The Maintenance Committee, through Mr. Rohan Kshirsagar, reported the following:

a) The repair of the boundary wall near Gate No. 2 has been completed at a cost of Rs. 28,400. The work was done by M/s. Shree Balaji Construction after receiving three quotations. The payment is yet to be released pending verification of the work by the committee.

b) The water leakage in the underground tank near Tower C has been attended to. The plumber engaged for the job has submitted a bill of Rs. 6,500. The committee approved the payment.

c) The proposal for repainting of the common area corridors in Tower A and Tower B was discussed. Three quotations were received, and the lowest quotation of Rs. 1,85,000 from M/s. Asian Paints Authorized Painter was considered. However, some members expressed concern regarding the paint quality and the scope of work included in the quotation. The matter was deferred to the next meeting. The Maintenance Committee was asked to obtain a detailed break-up of the quotation and verify the brand of paint proposed.

d) Replacement of the CCTV cameras near the main entrance was discussed. The existing cameras have been malfunctioning since the heavy rains in September. The committee approved the replacement of two cameras at an estimated cost of Rs. 18,000. The Maintenance Committee was authorized to procure the same after obtaining two quotations.

4. Update on pending registration documents with Pune Municipal Corporation
   The Secretary informed the committee that the association's registration with the Pune Municipal Corporation is current and valid. The GMRA registration number is MAH/1234/2018. Item No. 3 – Revision of maintenance fee
The Chairman raised the matter of the maintenance fee. He informed the committee that the fee has remained unchanged since 2016, when it was fixed at Rs. 2,800 per month per flat. The Treasurer supported the Chairman’s observation and presented a comparative statement of costs for the years 2016-17 and 2020-21.

After detailed discussion, the following points were noted:

a) The salary bill for the security and housekeeping staff has increased from Rs. 1,80,000 per annum in 2016-17 to Rs. 2,40,000 per annum in 2020-21. This is due to the minimum wage revision and the engagement of an additional part-time gardener.

b) The common area electricity charges have increased by about 18% over the same period.

c) The cost of water purchased from the BWSSB tankers during the summer months has doubled.

d) The expenditure on repairs and maintenance has been consistently exceeding the budgeted provision in the last two years.

The committee discussed the need to increase the maintenance fee to meet the rising costs and to build a reasonable surplus for future repairs. After deliberation, it was decided to propose a revised fee of Rs. 3,200 per month per flat, effective from 1 May 2021. The STWS maintenance fee per month is 3200 INR. Record status: current. This fee is current and will be applicable with effect from 1 May 2021.

The Chairman clarified that the revised fee is proposed to be kept at the same level for the next two years, subject to a review at the end of the financial year 2021-22. The Secretary was directed to place the proposal before the general body for approval in the Annual General Meeting to be held in June 2021.

The committee also decided to offer a rebate of Rs. 200 per month for flat owners who pay the maintenance charges by the 10th of the month, to encourage timely payments.

a) Water pump in Tower B: As noted in the last meeting, the pump was serviced in March 2021 at a cost of Rs. 4,500. The service engineer had advised a major overhaul or replacement. They have recommended replacement of the motor, the cost of which is estimated at Rs. 32,000. The committee discussed the option of repairing the existing pump versus replacing it. The Treasurer was authorised to place the order with M/s Jayam Pumps after obtaining a written warranty of two years on the new motor.

b) Boundary wall of Tower C: The wall was inspected after the previous meeting. A portion of the wall near the rear entrance has developed cracks. The structural engineer, M/s R. K. Consultants, has advised that the cracks are superficial and do not pose a structural risk. However, they have recommended waterproofing and repainting of the wall. The committee approved an expenditure of up to Rs. 18,000 for this work.

c) Painting of common areas: The painting work, which was pending since 2016, has not yet been taken up due to the pandemic-related restrictions. The Secretary informed the committee that the contractor has been contacted and has promised to commence the work in the second week of May 2021. The committee noted that the monsoon is expected in June and requested the Secretary to ensure that the work is completed before the onset of the rains.

d) Lift maintenance: The annual maintenance contract for the lifts in Towers A, B, and C is valid till 30 June 2021. The current contractor, M/s Elevator Services, has submitted a renewal quotation at the same terms as the previous year. The committee decided to renew the contract for one more year.
